subject: Temporary rate reprieve during quant rollout & SLA degradation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helium Health — quant rollout caused 99th pct SLA hits; asking for credit

Karthik —

Quick heads-up: Helium Health reported repeated 99th-pct latency spikes yesterday after we pushed the experimental 4-bit quantization profile to the model variant they use in production. Their telemetry shows tail latency breaches during batch peaks and they want commercial relief while we roll back / patch.

They're asking for a temporary concession while we stabilize: two options on the table from them — a 25% rate reduction for 60 days or a one-off credit equivalent to estimated overage (~$35k). They flagged this as an executive-level ask and want confirmation by EOD tomorrow.

Attached is their incident extract and our preliminary impact estimate (SLA-impact-estimate.xlsx). Product has a patch in progress but timeline is ~72 hours to roll back and add guardrails.

Can we get a quick decision on what to offer? If we need to submit to execs, I can prepare a short justification and commercial terms.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Exec — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Helium Health — quant rollout caused 99th pct SLA hits; asking for credit

Thanks for the write-up, Marissa.

A few thoughts up-front: we should treat this as a timeboxed commercial accommodation tied to clear mitigation milestones (rollback complete, patch validated, monitoring thresholds restored). I want finance to see the margin impact and product to commit to a short remediation plan.

Suggested ask from Sales (proposal to present to execs):
- One-off account credit: $25,000, OR
- Temporary rate reduction of 20% for 45 days (whichever is clearer contractually)
- Condition: rollback applied within 72 hours and weekly telemetry reports for 30 days post-fix

Michael — can you run the cost impact on both options and let me know preferred wording for the approval memo? Include any carveouts (e.g., not applied to overage credits from prior months).

Aditya — please draft a short mutual action plan with the customer (3 bullet milestones) so we can attach to the approval doc. I will pull this into an exec brief if finance flags actionable items.

If we need a formal exec signature I can route to Emily (CRO) with a 2-par paragraph asking.

Karthik
VP, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Karthik / Marissa —

Quick calc based on our current gross margins and the customer's committed ARR:
- Option A (one-off $25k credit): gross margin hit ~ $18.5k (after cost allocation).
- Option B (20% rate reduction, 45 days): estimate ~ $22k revenue delta (depends on usage cadence).

Recommendation: approve Option A (one-off credit) as it is cleaner to apply and closes faster from an accounting perspective. We should add a short recovery clause: if the rollback does not happen within 72 hours, the credit is rescinded and we revert to standard rates (customer-facing language required).

For exec memo I need a one-paragraph justification (what happened, why it's our responsibility, proposed remedy, and mitigation timeline) plus the mutual action plan Marissa/Aditya will add. Also confirm whether Sales needs the credit applied to the current invoice or as a separate billing credit (I prefer a billing credit entry).

I'll draft a short approval memo and circulate.

-Michael
Head of Finance Operations | Redwood Inference

Adding the mutual action plan draft below (keeps things short for execs):
1) Rollback quant profile to previous stable binary — target: within 72 hours of approval
2) Validate tail-latency in staging with production traffic replay and sign-off by Product — within 48 hours of rollback
3) Deliver weekly latency summary for 30 days; customer contact: Amir Qureshi

Customer ask preference: they indicated they prefer a rate reduction to simplify procurement approvals, but they also said a one-off credit would be acceptable. Given procurement timelines, I think offering the one-off credit with an option to convert to a short-term rate reduction for the next invoice might be politically simpler.

I'll prep a one-page handoff to Customer Success to manage the post-fix monitoring and will include the M.A.P. in the approval packet.

-Aditya

Subject: Exec approval requested: one-off credit for Helium Health (RDW-2027-HELIUM-42) — $25k

Emily —

As discussed with Sales and Finance, Helium Health experienced a tail-latency regression after an internal quantization rollout. Product is committed to a rollback + validation within 72 hours (see mutual action plan below). To preserve relationship and limit churn risk while we remediate, Sales recommends a one-off credit of $25,000 (Finance concurs).

Summary (one-paragraph for approval):
- What happened: experimental 4-bit quant profile triggered occasional KV-cache mis-sizing under peak batching, producing 99th-pct latency breaches for Helium Health's primary inference route.
- Why we own it: rollout configuration was selected in our shared runtime without the extra guardrails enabled for the customer's workload pattern.
- Remedy: one-off credit of $25k; rollback and patch to be completed within 72 hours; 30 days of telemetry reporting.

Mutual Action Plan (attached to approval):
1) Rollback to previous model binary — target T+72 hours
2) Product validation with replay traffic — T+120 hours
3) Weekly latency report for 30 days post-fix

Requested board/executive action: please sign to approve the credit and allow Sales to apply the credit as a billing credit on the next invoice. Approval links: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/sites/exec/approvals/HELIUM-42 (approval packet) and hubspot deal: https://hubspot.company/deals/HELIUM-42.

If approved, Marissa will confirm the mechanics with Procurement and I will notify CS to monitor the post-rollback window.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
